title: [Shortcut Guide] Taskbar indicators appear for all apps, instead of only when TASKBAR1-9 shortcuts are defined
summary: Shortcut Guide shows taskbar indicators for an app without TASKBAR1-9 shortcuts because the full-guide activation path refreshes taskbar layout after MainPane selection collapsed the pane.

status.label: Design fix candidate
status.detail: The report includes clear reproduction, a plausible code pointer, and source inspection confirms OverlayWindow.UpdateTaskbarPaneLayout ends by setting TaskbarPane.Visibility to Visible after MainPaneControl can signal that the selected app has no TASKBAR1-9 shortcuts.

next_action.label: Queue targeted Shortcut Guide fix design
next_action.reason: The issue appears localized to taskbar-pane visibility ownership after full-guide activation. Queue a focused design/fix workflow rather than asking for more reporter evidence.

judgment.rationale: The author supplied a concrete current-main repro and an implementation hypothesis. Focused source inspection supports the failure path: MainPaneControl determines that the selected app has no TASKBAR1-9 section and raises SelectedAppTaskbarVisibilityChanged(false), while OverlayWindow.UpdateTaskbarPaneLayout later sets TaskbarPane.Visibility = Visibility.Visible whenever taskbar layout exists.
evidence: The report reproduces on PowerToys 0.102 current main by focusing an app without TASKBAR1-9 shortcuts and triggering Shortcut Guide.
The actual screenshot shows both the main overlay and taskbar indicators.
MainPaneControl.SelectionChanged computes exposesTaskbarSection from shortcuts whose SectionName starts with <TASKBAR1-9> and raises SelectedAppTaskbarVisibilityChanged.
OverlayWindow.OnMainPaneTaskbarVisibilityChanged collapses TaskbarPane when shouldShow is false.
OverlayWindow.UpdateTaskbarPaneLayout collapses only when layout is null, otherwise positions the pane and sets TaskbarPane.Visibility to Visible.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused Shortcut Guide fix that separates taskbar layout refresh from taskbar visibility ownership, then add regression coverage for apps with and without TASKBAR1-9 shortcuts.

fix_assessment.rationale: A localized PowerToys fix is plausible and no existing public fix attempt covers this new Shortcut Guide taskbar-pane visibility regression.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep Shortcut Guide taskbar pane collapsed when the selected app exposes no taskbar shortcuts
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Taskbar pane visibility is owned by two paths: MainPaneControl correctly signals that the selected app lacks TASKBAR1-9 shortcuts, but UpdateTaskbarPaneLayout later makes the pane visible whenever taskbar layout exists.
plan: Move taskbar-pane visibility ownership out of UpdateTaskbarPaneLayout, or gate its final Visible assignment on the latest selected-app exposesTaskbarSection state.
Keep layout measurement/positioning available without forcing visibility for apps that do not expose TASKBAR1-9 shortcuts.
Ensure full-guide activation calls preserve the visibility decision made by MainPaneControl after the selected app manifest is loaded.
Add focused Shortcut Guide coverage for one app manifest with TASKBAR1-9 shortcuts and one without, verifying the taskbar pane is visible only for the former.
verification: Run Shortcut Guide unit/UI coverage for app selection and full-guide activation.

Manual check: focus Chrome or another app without TASKBAR1-9 shortcuts, trigger Shortcut Guide, and verify only the main overlay appears; then verify an app with TASKBAR1-9 shortcuts still shows taskbar indicators.

confidence.rationale: The issue report names the suspected method and source inspection confirms the competing visibility assignments. The remaining risk is choosing the least invasive state owner without regressing taskbar layout refresh.

issue_context.summary: Shortcut Guide displays taskbar indicators even when the selected application manifest has no TASKBAR1-9 shortcuts.
known_information: Installation method: dev build in Visual Studio.
The author reproduced by focusing Chrome, whose manifest does not define TASKBAR1-9 shortcuts, then triggering Shortcut Guide.
The author identified OverlayWindow.UpdateTaskbarPaneLayout as unconditionally setting TaskbarPane.Visibility to Visible.
inferences: The taskbar pane should follow the selected application manifest rather than raw taskbar layout availability.
The existing event path likely computes the right visibility, but a later layout refresh overrides it.
issue_context.analysis: This report has enough source-localized evidence for a targeted design/fix action. Asking for a bug report ZIP would not materially improve the decision because the failure is visible, current-main, and tied to deterministic Shortcut Guide control flow.
initial_investigation: Read the issue body, screenshot context, labels, assignee, and automated triage comment.
Inspected src/modules/ShortcutGuide/ShortcutGuide.Ui/ShortcutGuideXAML/Controls/MainPaneControl.xaml.cs and confirmed SelectedAppTaskbarVisibilityChanged is based on <TASKBAR1-9> shortcut sections.

Inspected src/modules/ShortcutGuide/ShortcutGuide.Ui/ShortcutGuideXAML/OverlayWindow.xaml.cs and confirmed UpdateTaskbarPaneLayout ends by setting TaskbarPane.Visibility to Visible when layout is non-null.
Inspected src/modules/ShortcutGuide/ShortcutGuide.Ui/ShortcutGuideXAML/App.xaml.cs and confirmed ShowFullGuide activation calls UpdateTaskbarPaneLayout.
